newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM sees 1997 inflation above 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM sees 1997 inflation above 8 pct.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Tuesday said he did not expect 1997 inflation to fall below eight percent, from its current level of more than nine percent.
Speaking after a meeting of economic ministers to discuss drafting the 1997 state budget Klaus said "Unfortunately we don't expect a number lower than eight (percent)."
He did not elaborate on whether he meant average or year-on-year inflation. For budget purposes, the government usually speaks in terms of average inflation.

Czech year-on-year inflation stood at 9.4 percent in July, while the moving average stood at 8.6 percent. The government in passing the 1996 budget forecast inflation for the year of roughly eight percent, but strong domestic demand has kept prices higher.
